signature_moves: Color-swatch-first toolbar: 5 annotation inks lead the bar before any tool, carrying the only saturation on an otherwise monochrome panel — color is the fastest live-annotation choice (Von Restorff)

Chrome engineered to float over the whole OS: the product is essentially just a dark borderless panel + a spotlight lens, designed to be invisible except its tools; opaque-dark (not glass) is the deliberate legibility choice for 'readable over any background'
Two-tier self-teaching settings rows: every control pairs a bold label with a full explanatory sentence, trading density for configure-once recognition
defects: Accent-binding tell (contested) — purple slider fill may be brand purple hardcoded over user's controlAccentColor; native apps bind controls to the user's accent; cannot disambiguate from a single still
Selection grammar unconfirmed — active tool/ink not legible on the toolbar in this composite
Accessibility floors unverifiable — 4.5:1 text, #14 focus, and >=24px hit targets on small glyphs cannot be checked from a low-res marketing composite (provenance ceiling, not a design fault)

aesthetic.direction: Split identity: committed single-hue purple consumer brand (drenched-color strategy on icon + marketing) wrapped around restrained monochrome utility chrome — closest range-map read is playful/consumer surface over an industrial/utilitarian toolbar

psychology: Von Restorff — the five saturated ink swatches pop against monochrome tools, making color the pre-attentively differentiated (and most-used) control
Fitts's Law — large tappable ink circles favor fast acquisition, but the small tool glyphs risk Target Starvation unless hit areas are padded (unverifiable here)
Recognition over recall — each settings row's explanatory sentence teaches the control inline, removing the need to remember what 'Spotlight Size' does
Jakob's Law — the AppKit icon-tab Preferences window is an instantly-familiar macOS pattern; zero learning cost
Hick's Law (correctly not applied) — a live-annotation tool palette is a scan surface, so ~7 tools + 5 colors kept visible is right; thinning it would hurt, not help
notes: Only input is a 1200x630 JPEG marketing composite (cover.jpg) — no standalone app shots (meta.json gallery/shots empty).
